positions.stance: Pledges to continue progress in "protecting vulnerable victims" and "ensuring justice for survivors of sexual abuse of all kinds."
Commits to "improving the quality of justice and building trust with our community."
Aims to redouble efforts to bring the community and law enforcement partners together "to address and prevent violence in our community."

or-clackamas-2026-clerk-mcmullen-catheri.name: Catherine McMullen
or-clackamas-2026-clerk-mcmullen-catheri.bio: Clackamas County Clerk since January 2023; former public librarian who launched a voter education and outreach program.

positions.stance: Will ensure every election is administered with integrity and transparency, with ballots processed securely and results reported on a consistent schedule.
Will expand access for eligible voters, including outreach to rural, young, disabled, and economically unstable voters and voters of color.
Will maintain and improve voter tools such as ballot tracking and technology that make participation easier and more secure.
Will continue officiating weddings for all couples and removing racist language from property records.

or-clackamas-2026-clerk-reaksecker-mark.name: Mark Reaksecker
or-clackamas-2026-clerk-reaksecker-mark.bio: Retired dentist who practiced for 32 years.

positions.stance: Calls for hand-counting all ballots instead of using vote tabulating machines, calling it accurate and less costly.
Supports verifying county voter rolls to remove deceased and out-of-county voters.
Proposes watermarking ballots so the clerk's office can verify that all ballots received are valid.
Opposes reporting partial vote results until all ballots are received.
Wants ballots arriving after election day tallied separately and compared with pre-election-day results.

or-clackamas-2026-sheriff-oneil-brad.name: Brad O'Neil
or-clackamas-2026-sheriff-oneil-brad.bio: Undersheriff with more than 27 years at the Clackamas County Sheriff's Office, from deputy to patrol captain.

positions.stance: Will make coverage and response times in rural and unincorporated communities "a measured priority, not an afterthought."
Calls a capable, well-equipped Search and Rescue and preparedness for wildfire and rural emergencies core to the mission.
Will lead an office that is visible, honest about how it operates, and accountable for its results.
Supports partnerships with local police and behavioral health providers, plus prevention work protecting families and property.
Will make recruitment and retention of deputies "a serious, sustained priority, not a line in a budget."

or-clackamas-2026-sheriff-rhodes-james.name: James Rhodes
or-clackamas-2026-sheriff-rhodes-james.bio: Appointed Clackamas County Sheriff; former patrol deputy, detective, police chief, and Undersheriff over 28 years in law enforcement.

positions.stance: "Start at the top. Protect the front line": find savings in administration first to protect deputies and services residents depend on.
Says budget decisions should begin with protecting public service, "not protecting bureaucracy."
Supports regular public budget reporting and quarterly updates so taxpayers can see whether the office stays on track.
Aims to improve response times, restore traffic and DUII enforcement, and follow up on property crimes.
Will target fentanyl dealers and drug traffickers while supporting programs that reduce crime and recidivism.

or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos2-sava.name: Paul Savas
or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos2-sava.bio: Clackamas County Commissioner and owner of the small business Savas Tuning Systems.

positions.stance: Supports safe, livable neighborhoods, strong public safety services, and investment in libraries, parks, and community spaces.
Promotes transparent decision-making and efficient, responsible use of taxpayer dollars.
Opposes ODOT's regional tolling plans and supports projects like the Sunrise Project and I-205 expansion.
Supports full funding for the County Sheriff's Office and emergency services.
Favors a business-friendly environment with balanced budgets and reasonable taxes, and support for small businesses and family-wage jobs.

or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos4-smit.name: R W Smith
or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos4-smit.bio: Environmental consultant serving on the Clackamas County Community Action Board and Community Climate Action Committee.

positions.stance: Opposes large-scale data centers in Clackamas County, citing electricity, water use, and loss of open space.
Wants to limit large corporations buying up housing and lower utility rates by building clean energy and ending data center subsidies.
Calls for more treatment options and shelter beds, and more affordable housing to prevent homelessness.
Says police and first responders must have the resources and tools they need to keep communities safe.

or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos4-helm.name: Diana Helm
or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos4-helm.bio: Clackamas County Commissioner appointed in 2025; small business owner and former Damascus mayor.

positions.stance: Says she is streamlining the permit process to accelerate new home construction.
Believes government "should empower, not hinder" local small businesses to grow living-wage jobs.
Prioritizes a justice system that works well for all citizens, with "compassion and accountability."
Will continue to advocate for the Sunrise Corridor so freight and residents can move safely through the county.

or-oregoncity-2026-mayor-marl-adam.name: Adam Marl
or-oregoncity-2026-mayor-marl-adam.bio: Oregon City Commissioner for five years and chair of the city's budget committee.

positions.stance: Opposes property tax increases, advocates reduced utility fees, and supports starter homes for young families and seniors.
Will prioritize fixing potholes and creating safe routes to school.
Prioritizes police funding, behavioral health, and accountable, compassionate regional efforts on homelessness.
Will prioritize investments in parks and continue supporting the library as a hub for literacy.
Supports reducing bureaucratic red tape and the city's small business grant programs.
Opposes spending city funds in court to "extinguish our right to vote on urban renewal."
Supports fully funded police by restoring tax dollars diverted to urban renewal.
Envisions a locally self-reliant economy, including a regional food hub and a North End solar energy district.
Proposes using Oregon's housing authority law to develop affordable starter cottage houses for young families.
If urban renewal remains, prioritize small-scale, high-impact projects citizens help design and construct.

or-oregoncity-2026-commissioner-lawrence.name: Gordon J Lawrence
or-oregoncity-2026-commissioner-lawrence.bio: Oregon City owner of an installation and renovation company; Historic Review Board volunteer.

positions.stance: Believes the city "can build what we need without sacrificing what makes us significant."
Says Oregon City should be a destination and will push policies to make it one.
Will push for Oregon City to invest in its parks, services, and infrastructure.

or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-guiney-brya.name: Bryan Guiney
or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-guiney-brya.bio: Lake Oswego Planning Commissioner and retired U.S. Marine.

positions.stance: Says "density belongs in centers and corridors, not imposed uniformly across established neighborhoods."
Supports policies to attract businesses, activate downtown and village centers, and allow adaptive reuse of older offices.
Prioritizes responsible budgeting, transparency, and long-range financial planning amid aging infrastructure costs.
Supports city employees while holding them accountable for responsive, high-quality services.

or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-walsh-patri.name: Patrick Walsh
or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-walsh-patri.bio: Nonprofit executive and former chair of the Lake Oswego Public Library Advisory Board.

positions.stance: Advocates sensible development that respects neighborhood character while meeting a growing community's needs.
Supports investing in smart, durable solutions for roads and utilities.
Wants every tax dollar managed with transparency and long-term vision.
Supports protecting lakes, parks, and the natural canopy.
Supports first responders to maintain a safe, welcoming city.

or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-miles-suzan.name: Suzanne Miles
or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-miles-suzan.bio: Former top appellate prosecutor for Oregon at the U.S. Department of Justice.

positions.stance: Sees opportunities for the city to partner with the school district, parents, and educators to keep schools thriving.
Values police and firefighters, calling public safety "the bedrock of a healthy city."
Wants to ensure the city takes care of its parks, waterways, and natural spaces as it grows.
Sees the city as a partner in helping local businesses thrive, including growing the Young Entrepreneur Program.
Supports firefighters and road-clearing staff and expanding emergency preparedness resources.
Calls for climate preservation plans and programs helping residents adopt environmentally friendly practices.
Supports prioritizing mental health first responders and education on unsafe gun storage and house fires.
Supports tracking collision data, expanding pedestrian, bike, and auto pathways, and prompt repairs.
Pledges to help assure realistic, sound budgeting for long-term city stability.

or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-tunmore-nei.name: Neil Tunmore
or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-tunmore-nei.bio: Retired Intel vice president after a 37-year career at the company.

positions.stance: Prioritizes schools and neighborhood safety, including safer walking routes around schools.
Wants to constantly maintain and improve infrastructure to attract families and new businesses.
Supports replacing grass with turf on public sports fields to increase usability.
Says "Salem oversteps with housing mandates" and wants them managed to conform to Lake Oswego building standards.
Calls for careful management of taxpayer money on projects like the North Anchor, fire station, sewer plant, and library.

or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-ramsey-heat.name: Heather Ramsey
or-lakeoswego-2026-councilor-ramsey-heat.bio: Runs an executive coaching and leadership development business; past chair of the Lake Oswego Chamber of Commerce.

positions.stance: Champions the local businesses that make Lake Oswego thrive.
Wants infrastructure improvements on time and on budget, with fiscally responsible visions for the Foothills and library.
Seeks to balance state housing mandates with local needs while preserving community character.
Supports safeguarding parks and waterways through environmental stewardship.
Supports police, fire, and emergency preparedness.

or-washington-2026-chair-fai-nafisa.name: Nafisa Fai
or-washington-2026-chair-fai-nafisa.bio: Washington County Commissioner and former commission vice chair; worked nearly a decade for the American Red Cross.

positions.stance: Will cut red tape by speeding up permits and simplifying regulations for small businesses.
Will increase housing supply, expand workforce housing, and invest in energy efficiency and utility assistance.
Will strengthen oversight, improve public access to information, and make county decision-making more open.
Will protect essential services and explore new revenue, including updated fees and local option levies, to close the budget gap.
"I will continue standing up to ICE and other federal overreach to protect Washington County."

or-washington-2026-chair-treece-pam.name: Pam Treece
or-washington-2026-chair-treece-pam.bio: Washington County Commissioner representing District 2 for eight years; former nonprofit leader.

positions.stance: Supports expanding housing choices, preserving affordable housing, and applying an affordability lens to county decisions.
Wants the county to live within its means, protect essential services, and evaluate programs based on results.
Will set expectations for a culture of respect, professionalism, and collaboration in county government.
Supports connecting people with shelter and housing while addressing addiction and behavioral health, with measurable results.
Supports local rent control indexed to inflation and streamlined zoning and permitting for mixed-use and multi-family homes.
Prioritizes the Beaverton Loop and TV Highway redevelopment, and supports longer-term WES expansion to Salem.
Supports transit-oriented development to densify downtown areas into pedestrian-centered spaces.
Would work to make Beaverton a gender-affirming care and abortion care sanctuary city.

or-beaverton-2026-council-pos1-philip-ra.name: Rachel Philip
or-beaverton-2026-council-pos1-philip-ra.bio: Software developer and former auditor; Central Beaverton Neighborhood Advisory Committee board member.

positions.stance: Supports policies that reduce financial pressures on residents while maintaining city services.
Will advocate for safe streets "no matter how you get around," including walking, biking, transit, and driving.
Committed to policies that prepare Beaverton for climate change and help residents reduce emissions.
Will connect residents who want to serve their city and help them navigate how to get involved.
Use the county's levers to improve transportation, coordinate across communities, and "help growth pay its fair share."
Bring residents into decisions earlier, explain tradeoffs, and report back on whether policies deliver.
Protect accessible voting, support transparent election administration, and pursue a citizen-led review of county representation.

ut-utah-2026-auditor-andersen-hans.name: Hans V. Andersen
ut-utah-2026-auditor-andersen-hans.bio: CPA with more than 40 years of experience and former Orem City Council member.

positions.stance: Pledges to "audit every dollar as if it were your own — because it is."
Will publish plain-English reports the average taxpayer can read.
Will "shine a light on debt before it's incurred, not after it's due."
Will treat every department, city, and business equally, with "no favorites, no exceptions."
Pledges to "answer to the people of Utah County, and no one else."
